text:
maria: Quick update — bringing up Notch22b-int4 on canary. Quant looks fine for quality but hitting slow generations when users request long responses (max_new_tokens > 256). Also saw 2 OOMs on a single host during a burst.

kevin: Can you paste the tail of the allocator logs? Which machine type?

maria: aws-g5-16x, here's the snippet:```
[2026-03-20T15:07:12Z] alloc: failed to reserve slot for kv cache (requested 1.2GB)
[2026-03-20T15:07:12Z] evict: trimming slots, freed 256MB
[2026-03-20T15:07:12Z] oom: process killed (out of device memory)
```

sophia: Two quick hypotheses: 1) default max_new_tokens=512 on the canary is allowing very long prefix+gen windows that blow past our kv reserve heuristics; 2) prefetch + continuous batching is inflating peak memory when many long jobs arrive.

ryan: Agreed. For Notch22b the int4 memory footprint is close to the edge on g5-16x once KV + prefetch are included. We should tighten the defaults for canary: lower max_new_tokens to 256 and reduce prefetch window to 32 tokens for this model.

maria: I can push a quick canary config change: `max_new_tokens: 256`, `prefetch: 32`, `batch_size_limit: 4` for the host pool. Any objections?

kevin: Also add a KV eviction policy tweak: decrease slot_reserve_ratio from 0.15 -> 0.08 for this model so we don't hold too much cold cache during bursts. We'll monitor impact on latency.

sophia: Add an automatic fallback policy to a 13B variant on OOM so user requests don't fail hard. `fallback_model: notch13b-lite`. Can infra-bot create an alert if OOM rate > 0.5%?

infra-bot: Alert rule created: `eng-ml.notch22b.oom_rate > 0.005 over 15m` -> notify #eng-oncall and #eng-ml.

maria: Plan: I'll deploy the canary config change now (small rollout), enable fallback and KV tweak. Then run a synthetic burst test with mixed short/long prompts (50% >200 tokens) and watch p95 latency and OOM counts.

kevin: For testing include this quick script to reproduce heavy KV pressure:```bash
for i in {1..80}; do 
  curl -sS -X POST $REDWOOD_URL/generate -d '{"model":"notch22b-int4","prompt":"${LOREM}","max_new_tokens":400}' &
done
wait
```

maria: launching now. Will report results in ~10m.

ryan: If OOMs persist after the config tweak, next step is to enable partial KV eviction (trim oldest 30%) on allocation failure and lower continuous-batcher max_concurrent_batches from 12 -> 6. That will hurt throughput but preserve latency SLOs.

maria: Result: after change, synthetic burst completed with 0 OOMs, p95 reduced from 620ms -> 410ms, tail memory usage dropped ~18%. Leaving canary config in place and rolling to 3 more hosts.

sophia: Nice. Follow-up: add a docs note under model catalog recommending conservative max_new_tokens defaults for int4 quantized 20B+ models and link to onboarding checklist (kv/reserve, prefetch, fallback).

kevin: I'll open a tiny PR to the catalog. Thanks team :thumbsup:
